deckTitle: The Move: A Field Guide to Managed Reactions

cards.power: Frames an existing condition as immediate and universal to justify a response not otherwise available.
cards.lore: The condition may predate the framing; the urgency is introduced when the response requires it.
cards.gradeReason: Instantly playable: you know exactly whose role you're inhabiting and what you're doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vintage propaganda poster. Subject: Bureaucrat raccoon pressing emergency button over mundane scene. Mood: Performative urgency masking routine.

cards.power: Sustains alertness toward dangers whose evidence cannot be independently examined.
cards.lore: Vigilance is maintained for threats described as classified, structural, or too complex to summarize.
cards.gradeReason: Role is clear but threat-type needs table context to perform convincingly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cold war security briefing graphic. Subject: Owl guard watching empty darkness from surveillance tower. Mood: Tense, vigilant, uneasy.

cards.power: Extends emergency framing into adjacent domains as each measure reveals new requirements.
cards.lore: The original threat remains formally unresolved while response infrastructure enters areas it never initially addressed.
cards.gradeReason: The metastasizing crisis — you know immediately what to embody and how to spread.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Infographic gone wrong. Subject: Crisis zone map consuming neighboring territories like spreading ink blot. Mood: Administrative creep, bureaucratic appetite.

cards.power: Converts a temporary emergency designation into stable infrastructure once adaptation removes the pressure to remove it.
cards.lore: The emergency expires; the systems built under it are now the standard and are no longer described as temporary.
cards.gradeReason: One of the corpus's best cards. 'The emergency is over. The systems remain.' Plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Retro government brochure. Subject: Emergency sign rusted and overgrown, still labeled TEMPORARY. Mood: Resigned permanence, forgotten urgency.

cards.power: Channels existing frustration toward a specific named target at a specific moment.
cards.lore: Diffuse dissatisfaction acquires an address; the structural conditions producing it do not.
cards.gradeReason: Pure performance: give the crowd a name, not a system. You know your move immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Revolutionary poster. Subject: Bull with microphone aiming crowd's energy at a single named figure. Mood: Controlled fury, choreographed rage.

cards.power: Concentrates distributed accountability onto a single identifiable figure.
cards.lore: A name is provided; the structural conditions that produced the outcome are not named in the same sentence.
cards.gradeReason: Ancient archetype, immediately embodiable. A name. Not a system.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Medieval trial illustration. Subject: Single goat in the dock surrounded by pointing fingers. Mood: Ritual sacrifice, institutional convenience.

cards.power: Converts directed anger into a self-sustaining cycle that requires no further external input.
cards.lore: Each event in the cycle increases receptivity to the next; the cycle no longer needs curating.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanism but the self-sustaining loop role is harder to embody without setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1980s PSA aesthetic. Subject: Hyena watching TV that shows the hyena watching TV. Mood: Self-sustaining alarm, no beginning or end.

cards.power: Produces a population sorted into opposed groups whose primary energy flows toward each other rather than outward.
cards.lore: Attention concentrates on the division; the mechanism that produced it operates outside the frame.
cards.gradeReason: Sort the room into camps, harvest the friction. The operator's role is crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Political cartoon. Subject: Machine sorting animals into two cages, energy arcing between cages. Mood: Harvest of opposition, engineered division.

cards.power: Saturates available processing capacity through volume, making navigation more expensive than the decision it informs.
cards.lore: Navigation requires more effort than most content costs; the destination is reached by fewer than the distribution implies.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanism is vivid but the performance role of 'the flooder' needs scaffolding to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Overwhelmed editorial desk. Subject: Beaver drowning in documents while trying to find one specific memo. Mood: Volume as weapon, navigation as cost.

cards.power: Places credentialed opposing voices on each contested question until no stable factual baseline holds.
cards.lore: For each position, peer-reviewed counter-information is available at identical distribution.
cards.gradeReason: Concept sharp but 'produce a contradiction field' needs a specific domain to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Academic debate visual. Subject: Two parrots at podiums citing each other's sources in opposite directions. Mood: Peer-reviewed impasse, credentialed standoff.

cards.power: Distributes authority across subspecialties until no synthesizing voice is structurally available.
cards.lore: The question requires cross-domain assessment; the institution that would coordinate that assessment has not been organized.
cards.gradeReason: Structural description with no clear character to embody. Who performs this? Unclear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Org chart nightmare. Subject: Owls in siloed offices each holding one puzzle piece, no table in sight. Mood: Structural incompleteness, coordinated absence.

cards.power: Converts unresolvable information load into passive acceptance of the default already in place.
cards.lore: After sufficient exposure to contradictory authoritative claims, people stop choosing and accept what is already there.
cards.gradeReason: STANDARD DEFAULT OPTION — ACCEPT ALL DEFAULTS. The sloth knows exactly what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Consumer UX design. Subject: Sloth before infinite form, checkboxes pre-ticked ACCEPT ALL DEFAULTS. Mood: Exhausted consent, manufactured passivity.

cards.power: Introduces genuine support that gradually becomes the only available path for the need it serves.
cards.lore: The service is real; the dependency it produces is a structural output, not a design flaw.
cards.gradeReason: The 'genuine care that becomes a trap' role needs table orientation — not instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Welfare state pastoral. Subject: Sheep given food from fence that is also the fence keeping them in. Mood: Genuine care, structural dependency.

cards.power: Conditions essential access on continued enrollment, making exit structurally expensive.
cards.lore: Leaving the system means losing access that was built only through being inside it.
cards.gradeReason: The fox who controls the exit. You know exactly who you are the moment you read the title.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate lobby. Subject: Fox in suit at turnstile, holding keys to the elevator. Mood: Essential access, managed exit.

cards.power: Converts one-time transactions into recurring relationships requiring active effort to exit.
cards.lore: The service is unchanged; the delivery model ensures return and places exit responsibility on the user.
cards.gradeReason: Economic mechanism clear, but 'perform the subscription state' needs specificity to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Packaging design parody. Subject: Squirrel buried under ACORN-SUB boxes arriving forever. Mood: Recurring obligation, friction-gated exit.

cards.power: Expands available choices within the system while the practical infrastructure for choices outside it contracts.
cards.lore: Freedom of movement within the system increases as the conditions for movement outside it quietly contract.
cards.gradeReason: 'Free within the cage, caged outside' — the image and the role arrive simultaneously.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Architectural diagram. Subject: Bird in large ornate cage with many perches, door to outside sealed shut. Mood: Apparent choice, contained horizon.

cards.power: Ties self-concept to membership until belonging becomes a structural rather than voluntary condition.
cards.lore: The group provides genuine benefits; those benefits become reasons not to evaluate the group on its own terms.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanism is right but it's a state, not a role — needs a character angle to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Community mural. Subject: Animals bonded in circle, gate visible but everyone facing inward. Mood: Genuine belonging, structural blindspot.

cards.power: Introduces visible periodic tests that sort members from non-members without stating the evaluation criteria.
cards.lore: The content of the test matters less than the visible act of passing it.
cards.gradeReason: The enforcer who tests without explaining the criteria. You perform this the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Secret society initiation. Subject: Raccoon performing ritual, surrounding animals watching for errors they won't name. Mood: Earned uncertainty, visible sorting.

cards.power: Converts private doubt into required public display of certainty as the currency of membership.
cards.lore: Public performance of belief becomes required; private disagreement is present but quiet.
cards.gradeReason: Display certainty. Doubt privately. The performance is the card. Immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate ID card. Subject: Badger displaying CERTIFIED BELIEVER pin while eyes say otherwise. Mood: Public performance, private doubt.

cards.power: Accumulates relationships, infrastructure, and identity inside the group until leaving means losing several things that cannot be recovered simultaneously.
cards.lore: The exit cost was not imposed as a penalty. It accrued through ordinary participation.
cards.gradeReason: Devastating. 'It accrued through ordinary participation' is the entire play in one sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Moving day disaster. Subject: Animal tangled in web of relationships and identity, all connected to one address. Mood: Accumulated belonging, impossible departure.

cards.power: Establishes a preferred behavior through expectation rather than requirement.
cards.lore: The behavior is formally optional; consequences for non-compliance distribute informally and consistently.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanism is solid but 'expectation as enforcement' needs a specific domain to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Public health campaign. Subject: Owl teacher gesturing toward STRONGLY ENCOURAGED box, consequences implied. Mood: Optional that isn't, expectation as enforcement.

cards.power: Uses observed compliance as the primary evidence that compliance is correct.
cards.lore: The behavior spreads because it is visible; the reasoning behind it is rarely articulated.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanism but the role of 'the person who sees the cascade' lacks a sharp performance hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mid-century crowd behavior study. Subject: Line of groundhogs following the one in front, first one invisible. Mood: Visible compliance as evidence, cascade without origin.

cards.power: Arranges the choice architecture so the preferred option requires measurably less friction than alternatives.
cards.lore: The choice is genuinely available; the costs of choosing against the design accumulate in small unannounced increments.
cards.gradeReason: Design-thinking concept. The EFFORTLESS PATH image helps but role isn't instantly embodyable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Choice architecture diagram. Subject: Donkey facing escalator vs. stairs labeled CAUTION HIGH FRICTION. Mood: Genuine choice, tilted terrain.

cards.power: Produces consistent behavioral alignment through distributed informal costs that are never announced.
cards.lore: No mandate was issued. No penalty was declared. The behavior is consistent.
cards.gradeReason: Punish without announcing the punishment. The role is immediately clear and immediately chilling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate performance review. Subject: Fox receiving smaller desk, worse coffee, quieter room — no paperwork changes. Mood: Distributed cost, announced nothing.

cards.power: Determines which context a fact arrives with before the fact can be examined independently.
cards.lore: The same event produces distinct public understanding depending on the surrounding material — which is selected.
cards.gradeReason: The editor who chooses what surrounds the story. Role and move arrive together.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Editorial room. Subject: Raven editor choosing surrounding photos, story itself unchanged. Mood: Curatorial power, invisible selection.

cards.power: Aligns multiple institutional voices around a single interpretation in the same window of time.
cards.lore: The alignment is described as independent consensus; its timing is documented and rarely explained.
cards.gradeReason: Coordination mechanism is clear but the performer's role needs more specificity to execute at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Broadcasting tower graphic. Subject: Multiple animals at separate microphones reading same script, clocks showing same time. Mood: Coordinated consensus, undocumented timing.

cards.power: Converts a claim into familiarity through repetition, and familiarity into assumed truth.
cards.lore: The claim does not become verified; it becomes recognizable — which produces a similar effect.
cards.gradeReason: Say it again. Familiarity is proof. The parrot knows exactly what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Propaganda parrot training manual. Subject: Parrot repeating phrase until crowd nods as if it's confirmed. Mood: Familiarity as verification, repetition as proof.

cards.power: Allows contradicting information to become inaccessible without active removal.
cards.lore: The prior account was not deleted; the new account was placed higher, in larger type, in more locations, for longer.
cards.gradeReason: TOP RESULT / LATEST / FEATURED — the move is visible in the visual alone. Instant play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Search engine results mockup. Subject: OLD STORY buried under TOP RESULT / LATEST / FEATURED in same font. Mood: Active displacement, passive disappearance.

cards.power: Introduces change at a rate calibrated to fall below the threshold that reliably triggers active resistance.
cards.lore: Each step is unremarkable; the cumulative distance becomes significant only when measured from the original position.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanism is vivid but 'be the gradual shift' is a process, not a character — harder to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Scientific measurement diagram. Subject: Frog in pot, thermometer rising, previous water temperature measurement crossed out. Mood: Unremarkable steps, remarkable distance.

cards.power: Converts an exceptional condition into the standard through sustained repetition and adaptation.
cards.lore: After sufficient time, the exception is no longer described as exceptional.
cards.gradeReason: State change clearly described but needs a performer's hook — who says 'this is normal now'?
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Government standards publication. Subject: EXCEPTIONAL line crossed out, NEW NORMAL line drawn at same level. Mood: Administrative normalization, quiet redefinition.

cards.power: Produces explanations that position the current state as the natural or inevitable outcome.
cards.lore: The trajectory is legible only toward the current position; alternative paths are no longer narrated as having been possible.
cards.gradeReason: The spin doctor who makes history inevitable. 'It was always going this way' is the entire character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Historical documentary aesthetic. Subject: Badger rewriting map arrows to point only where they already went. Mood: Inevitable trajectory, illegible alternatives.

cards.power: Converts sufficient duration into apparent permanence, and apparent permanence into natural fact.
cards.lore: Those who arrived after the shift describe the current state as normal. Those who arrived before it are fewer.
cards.gradeReason: 'Those who remember the before are fewer now.' Devastating and immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Generational photograph. Subject: Young animals explaining to elders that this is how it has always been. Mood: Demographic replacement of memory, normalized reality.

cards.power: Introduces a sudden cost increase that disrupts established behavior before alternatives can be organized.
cards.lore: The shock produces rapid adaptation; the adapted state accepts the new cost structure as the baseline.
cards.gradeReason: SHOCK! CRASH! HIKE! — the card art screams the move. You disrupt behavior before alternatives form.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Supermarket receipt nightmare. Subject: Fox staring at receipt: SHOCK CRASH HIKE items. Mood: Rapid behavioral disruption, forced adaptation.

cards.power: Reduces — or appears to reduce — the supply of an essential good to redirect behavior at scale.
cards.lore: Scarcity may be real or managed; the behavioral response is structurally identical in either case.
cards.gradeReason: Key insight (real vs. managed scarcity, identical response) but the performance role needs framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Supply chain diagram. Subject: Raven controlling pipeline valve, queue of animals stretching out of frame. Mood: Behavioral redirection, managed shortage.

cards.power: Converts future income into present compliance through obligation structures accepted under prior conditions.
cards.lore: The harness is taken on voluntarily at a specific moment; the future it governs was not fully legible at that moment.
cards.gradeReason: Economic mechanism precise and true — but 'be the debt harness' is structural, not instantly performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian workhouse illustration. Subject: Horse harnessed to cart labeled FUTURE INCOME, signed at one past moment. Mood: Future sold at moment of need, governance through obligation.

cards.power: Reduces the real value of resources incrementally while the nominal value remains constant.
cards.lore: The number is the same. The quantity it purchases is smaller. The adjustment is continuous, distributed, and unremarkable.
cards.gradeReason: The three-sentence lore is perfect. The performance role is subtle — economist-as-magician needs setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Economic chart parody. Subject: Squirrel holding same coin, mountain of goods it used to buy now shrinking. Mood: Nominal stability, real erosion.

cards.power: Makes the preferred option sufficiently easier than alternatives until alternatives become effectively unavailable over time.
cards.lore: The alternative remained technically accessible; the friction required to reach it accumulated into practical impossibility.
cards.gradeReason: Clear UX-as-control mechanism. The performer's role needs a scene to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: UX funnel diagram. Subject: Raccoon standing before immediate preferred path vs. very long alternative route. Mood: Frictionless capture, accumulated unavailability.

cards.power: Replaces human decision points with automated processes that cannot be questioned on the same terms as human decisions.
cards.lore: Responsibility for the outcome follows the system's design rather than the system's output.
cards.gradeReason: 'It's the algorithm' — accountability routed through machines. Immediately performative tech-defense role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Tech company aesthetic. Subject: Machine stamping PROCESSED on decisions, human hands removed from the chain. Mood: Algorithmic accountability displacement, systemic responsibility.

cards.power: Produces consequential outcomes through processes whose criteria are inaccessible to those they affect.
cards.lore: The decision stands; the criteria are proprietary; an appeal is available at significant time and cost.
cards.gradeReason: Administrative opacity well described — but the role of 'the black box operator' needs more edge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Administrative tribunal. Subject: Raccoon receiving verdict from sealed box, APPEAL button visible, line around the building. Mood: Opaque authority, accessible in theory.

cards.power: Shapes available action through design until the design becomes the perceived space of possibility.
cards.lore: Users describe their choices as free; the choices listed were those that remained after the design was finalized.
cards.gradeReason: UX-as-politics is sharp, but the performance role of 'the designer who constrains' needs scene-setting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: UX wireframe. Subject: Hamster at touchscreen — all buttons visible, all grayed out except the default. Mood: Designed limitation, experienced as choice.

cards.power: Attaches institutional credentialing to a position, elevating its authority above independent examination.
cards.lore: The seal confirms expertise; it also confirms institutional alignment with the body that issued it.
cards.gradeReason: The owl stamps approval, and the stamp bears the owl's employer's logo. Instantly playable credentializer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Official certification. Subject: Owl with institutional stamp, stamp bearing the owl's employer's crest. Mood: Credentialed alignment, circular validation.

cards.power: Circulates an aligned position through multiple institutional channels until simultaneous publication registers as independent consensus.
cards.lore: The positions arrived at similar conclusions within the same period; any coordination is not documented.
cards.gradeReason: The mechanism is sharp but the performer's role ('be the echo') is distributed — hard to embody solo.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Press release distribution. Subject: Same document arriving on different letterheads simultaneously in multiple inboxes. Mood: Coordinated consensus, described as independent.

cards.power: Converts oversight institutions into endorsement institutions through sustained personnel and incentive alignment.
cards.lore: The regulator was designed to monitor the industry; over a sufficient period, the industry shaped the regulator.
cards.gradeReason: The industry fox now wearing the regulator's hat. Classic role, classic move. Zero setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Nature documentary. Subject: Industry fox wearing regulator's hat, regulator's desk now empty. Mood: Structural substitution, timeline compressed.

cards.power: Maintains the visible form of accountability while the functional capacity for it is structurally unavailable.
cards.lore: The committee convenes; the questions are asked; the record is complete; the practice continues.
cards.gradeReason: The committee convenes. The cameras roll. The record is complete. The practice continues. Play it verbatim.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Congressional hearing aesthetic. Subject: Committee of animals with cameras, subject continues unchanged behind them. Mood: Record complete, practice continues.

cards.power: Redirects attention from a position's content to the credibility of its source.
cards.lore: The argument is not answered; the arguer's qualifications, history, or associations are examined instead.
cards.gradeReason: Attack the arguer, not the argument. The foam finger is the performance. Instant and vicious.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Debate club gone wrong. Subject: Badger pointing foam finger at opponent's biography, opponent's argument visible on board behind. Mood: Source over substance, arguer over argument.

cards.power: Removes the visible social infrastructure around a position until it appears to stand alone.
cards.lore: Others who hold the position become quiet; it appears fringe when it describes something widely experienced.
cards.gradeReason: Powerful observation — but 'be the isolation effect' is a slow structural play, not a sharp table move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Social network topology diagram. Subject: Fox on island, bridges retracted, position unchanged, appearance: fringe. Mood: Structural isolation, manufactured marginality.

cards.power: Routes a position from high-distribution channels to low-visibility ones without formal suppression.
cards.lore: The position continues; it reaches a fraction of the prior audience; it no longer affects consensus-forming conversations.
cards.gradeReason: NOISE vs. TRUTH image is strong. The performer's role ('route it quietly') needs a platform to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Broadcast signal diagram. Subject: Speaker moving from stadium to small room to whisper — content unchanged, reach decimated. Mood: Position demoted, audience restructured.

cards.power: Converts the cost of contesting suppression into a structural disincentive for future challenges.
cards.lore: The case matters; it requires years and resources beyond most challengers; the effect on future challengers is structural.
cards.gradeReason: Make the fight itself the punishment. The filing cabinet tower says it all. Sharp and playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Court filing diagram. Subject: Small challenger at courthouse entrance vs. tower of boxes labeled YEARS 1 through 7. Mood: Process as punishment, structure as deterrent.

cards.power: Converts external behavioral requirements into internal monitoring, removing the need for visible enforcement.
cards.lore: The behavior is maintained without surveillance because the person no longer registers its absence.
cards.gradeReason: Panopticon internalized — correct and important. But 'play the self-policing loop' needs interiority to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Panopticon diagram. Subject: Dog in empty room watching surveillance camera that may or may not be on. Mood: Internalized monitoring, surveillance made redundant.

cards.power: Binds behavioral compliance with self-concept until non-compliance requires personal revision.
cards.lore: The behavior is no longer performed for the institution; it is performed for who the participant understands themselves to be.
cards.gradeReason: 'Compliance becomes who you are.' This is the deep game. You embody it in one breath.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mirror portrait. Subject: Raccoon looking in mirror — compliance badge reflection is also the face. Mood: Behavioral fusion, self-concept as infrastructure.

cards.power: Converts a history of failed attempts to affect outcomes into a stable belief that outcomes cannot be affected.
cards.lore: The belief was rational given the prior evidence; it persists after the evidence changes.
cards.gradeReason: The dog who stopped trying. EXIT visible. Evidence changed. Still sitting. Instantly embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Psychology experiment aesthetic. Subject: Dog in empty room with clearly visible EXIT, sitting still, having learned it doesn't open. Mood: Rational surrender, outdated evidence.

cards.power: Produces consistent alignment without enforcement because the system's requirements have been adopted as personal values.
cards.lore: At this stage, no enforcement is required. The participants carry it for free.
cards.gradeReason: Best card in the deck. 'No enforcement required. The participants carry it for free.' Table-ready at any level.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mass movement documentary. Subject: Crowd of animals in uniform marching — no officers anywhere visible. Mood: Adopted requirement, enforcement made unnecessary.

cards.power: Frames the identification of a recurring structure as evidence of interpretive error rather than pattern recognition.
cards.lore: Naming the structure is described as projection; the structure continues while the naming is contested.
cards.gradeReason: 'Naming the pattern is proof you're wrong.' The role of the Denier is crisp and immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Scientific skepticism pamphlet. Subject: Raccoon presenting clear pattern chart, duck across table describing it as coincidence. Mood: Pattern as pathology, recognition as error.

cards.power: Maintains that repeated outcomes in the same direction are each individually and separately explicable.
cards.lore: Every instance has a different explanation; the explanation for the pattern is that there is no pattern.
cards.gradeReason: Important observation but 'perform the coincidence stack' is abstract — harder to anchor at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Conspiracy board parody. Subject: Owl calmly explaining each red string connection as unrelated individual events. Mood: Credentialed denial, sustained explainer.

cards.power: Uses the genuine complexity of systems to make pattern description appear naive or incomplete.
cards.lore: The system is genuinely complex; what it consistently produces is not.
cards.gradeReason: The academic who deploys real complexity to hide a simple output. Immediately embodiable expert-obfuscator.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Academic chalkboard. Subject: Beaver in lab coat filling board with equations — behind: simple arrow going one direction. Mood: Genuine complexity, deliberately deployed.

cards.power: At sufficient scale of internalization, the pattern no longer needs to be performed — it becomes the ambiance.
cards.lore: The move is complete when it stops being a move and becomes the environment.
cards.gradeReason: The perfect closer. When the move disappears into reality, the game is over. You know it when you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ambiance photography. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit in normal urban scene, every element quietly labeled with its move. Mood: Structural ubiquity, named at last.

verdict: The Move is what happens when investigative journalism meets game design and neither one blinks first. Fourteen chapters, fifty-six patterns of managed reality — and not one of them requires a villain, just a sequence that repeated. Named strength: the ★ capstone cards (The Voluntary Compliance, The Move Itself, The Permanent Exception) are some of the sharpest writing in the entire Kayfabizarro corpus. Named weakness: a few mechanism-heavy cards in The Fog Machine and The Default sections describe structural processes without a clear character to embody — they're true but harder to play. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 patterns of managed consent — from emergency manufacturing to voluntary compliance. For journalists, researchers, and anyone who's noticed the pattern but couldn't name it yet. A field guide, not a conspiracy theory.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob in full chaos-operator mode flanked by glowing CRT banks, BLÖDSINN! sign overhead, cockroaches below — maximum visual energy
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'THE MOVE: A Field Guide to Managed Reactions' is one of the best cover titles in the corpus; scope and tone arrive in one sentence
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — chaos-awareness-field-guide energy matches the deck's investigative taxonomy perfectly
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — nothing else in the project frames itself as a field guide to managed reactions; the framing is fresh and immediately credible
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — 'A Field Guide to Managed Reactions' is a phrase that travels; it sounds like a book that already exists and should
coverQA.coverNote: This cover is doing everything right. The taglines do the work before anyone opens the deck: 'The pattern doesn't need you to believe in it. It needs you to not name it.' That's a hook and a thesis simultaneously. FrizzleBob's panic energy paired with the clinical subtitle is the correct tension for this material.

notes: 14 thematic sections, each with 3 setup cards + 1 star capstone card. Section headers function as meta-cards and could be printed as standalone dividers. Each section has axis labels (e.g., URGENCY/CONTROL, ANARCHY LITE/VOID) that create a spatial map of the mechanism. The star capstone cards are consistently stronger than the setup cards — the deck rewards being played section by section. Card 9 (Information Flood) lore was partially obscured in the layout; reconstructed from context. Companion deck 'THE_MOVE_(1)' already in corpus — recommend cross-referencing for bundle placement. No font artifacts observed; text appears cleanly typeset throughout. KayfaBINGO!/KayfaBOGGLE!/KayfaBIZARRO! bonus tags appear on several pages as in-joke reward layers.

quickWins: Print section header titles as standalone meta-cards — they read as well as the regular cards
The Coincidence Stack lore is the weakest in the deck — tighten the second sentence
Cross-reference with THE_MOVE_(1) to establish vol.1/vol.2 relationship in SSOT
niceToHave: Consider a 'Counter-Move' expansion where each card gets an opposing play
The Complexity Shield could use a stronger visual — the chalkboard is functional but generic for such a sharp card
Bundle with Deep State Plumbing, Federal Kayfabe, and KAYFABIZARRO REDACTED for a Systems of Control quartet

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE MOVE – A Field Guide to Managed Reactions (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The pattern only works while nobody says its name out loud. So let's say all fifty-six.

Here is the sequence, stripped of its costume. An alarm goes off and urgency walks in the door. The outrage gets pointed somewhere useful. A complexity shield goes up so no single person can ever be held to the floor. Oversight theater runs a matinee while the real decision was made before the doors opened. By the final beat nobody coerced you into anything. You comply on your own, you thank the room for the option, and you call it a choice. Fourteen sections, fourteen moments where the trick quietly changes hands, one repeatable machine that has been run on you more times than you have names for it.

The Move is a Social Story Wrestling deck pointed at the mechanism of control itself. You do not study the tactic from a safe distance. You pick up the card, perform the move out loud with a straight face, and the table rules whether anyone in the room would have caught it in the wild.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Move Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards across 14 sections, featuring The Voluntary Compliance, The Permanent Exception, and The Oversight Theater.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the Name-the-Pattern call that closes every round.
- The Control Map: every section sits on its own axis, from Urgency against Control to Anarchy-Lite against Void, so the full deck reads as a floor plan of how managed reality gets built.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this deck and you are not buying a static PDF. You are on the list. Every future section, capstone card, and topic-specific expansion in this cycle lands in your library as a free update.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because a pattern you can name is a pattern that loses its grip on you. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Run it. Name the thing the next time it walks past you in a headline. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and mapping the next sections.
Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"If you can name the pattern, you can see it again."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
